newsitem.title: USA: Connie Lee Insurance hires five, begins expansion.
newsitem.headline: Connie Lee Insurance hires five, begins expansion.

text.p: Connie Lee Insurance Co. said Monday it hired five municipal bond insurance professionals as part of the company's new expansion.

James Gerry, Joseph Lebenson and Bruce Worner joined Connie Lee's public finance department as vice presidents and managers. Gregory Aikman is a new assistant vice president for surveillance, and William deSante Jr. will be a part-time consultant, the company said.

Connie Lee also announced Monday it had begun operating as a primary insurer in all sectors of the municipal market. The U.S. Congress authorized Connie Lee's expansion beyond the health care and higher education sectors, as part of a recently completed privatization of the company.

"These appointments are a confirmation of our commitment to serve a broader spectrum of the municipal marketplace with the addition of talented, experienced individuals who will apply their specialized expertise to new market sectors," Oliver Sockwell, president and chief executive officer of Connie Lee, said in a statement.

Gerry is vice president and manager of underwriting for tax-backed, utility, transportation and special revenue sectors in the Southern region. He was previously a manager at MBIA Insurance Corp., a unit of MBIA Inc.

Lebenson is a vice president for the same sectors in the Northern sector. He was previously a vice president at Financial Guaranty Insurance Co., a unit of GE Capital Services, the General Electric Co subsidiary.

Worner is manager of secondary market activity at Connie Lee. He was previously a vice president at Capital Guaranty Insurance Co. Aikman, assistant vice president of surveillance, was also previously at Capital Guaranty.
deSante was a managing director at Moody's Investors Service Inc., where he focused on structured finance, bond insurance, and several other sectors.
